## **Abstract**

## **Introduction**

In the present paper, it is carried out the design of a photovoltaic installation connected to the utility grid with panels mounted on a floating structure at an irrigator’s community. The objective is to determine the technical and economic feasibility of a floating photovoltaic installation to partially or totally cover the energy demand.

The floating photovoltaic technology modality provides better production yields in photovoltaic panels since they are kept in natural refrigeration and at lower temperatures than if they were mounted on a roof. Its use for irrigation facilities is attractive if an irrigator pool nearby is available. However, the cost of installing floating structures is considerably higher compared to a similar photovoltaic installation on a roof. For the design of the proposed system, 272 PV panels with a 108 kW peak installed and a 100 kW inverter are used. The electrical calculations are also carried out to size all the installation wiring and incorporate the corresponding protections to guarantee a safe operation. The total cost of the photovoltaic installation is 119,100 €. The photovoltaic generation is 188 MWh/year, covering 13.6% of the energy demand.

## **Keywords**

Photovoltaic system, floating, renewable energy, self-consumption, compensation.

The floating PV (FPV) is a technology which has been spreading, mainly from 2015, from them which the growth has been almost exponential. The main countries with this type of facilities are mainly Asian in origins, such as China, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, investment in the United States, France and the Netherlands is also growing. This technology has increased in the renewable energy market since 2016.  In December 2018, it reached 1.3 GW of installed power. [1]  [2]

Floating PV plant provides benefits such as a) water helps to keep panels at low temperatures, b) the problem of shading is not present in the case of an FPV plant, c) there is a reduction in the growth of algae on water, d) no fixed structure is presented in the case of an FPV plant (installation can be reversible) [1] e) evaporation of water is reduced by 80 % as it is covered by floating platforms [3].

Several papers assess Floating PV system [4] [5] [6].  The installation of large-scale PV systems has substantial requirements on land usage; approximately 1.6 ha of land per each MW installed [7]. Also since land resources are scarce their acquisition cost is higher, impacting the economic viability of projects negatively. In this context, FPV emerges as a solution to mitigate the challenges due to lack of space, as it will use idle areas, avoiding conflicts, for example, with agricultural use [8].

In this paper, Homer and SAM are used to estimate the energy production and to carry out economic analysis. However other tools can be used. Recent studies show models and methods for PV systems in which are evidenced more accurate results for simulation models; by considering environmental weather conditions, PV system architecture, interactions of PV components with the weather conditions, manufacturing quality,  materials used and combinations with other sources such a wind systems. [9] [10] [11]

In this paper, the results of the design of an FPV system are presented. The structure of the manuscript is composed of the methodology, energy demand, solar resource, devices used, calculations, scheme of the system and results.

## **II. Description of the installation**

The Cooperative of Irrigators, located in the Valencia Region, supplies 717 hectares of fields dedicated to the cultivation of citrus and

vegetables. At its head station is the pumping system that distributes the water resource to the required areas. The water is stored in a reservoir of 16,640 m[3] and it is derived to the fields through 3 pumps in parallel, whose operation is governed by a control system that guarantees the necessary irrigation in all sectors.

## Irrigation Shifts

The irrigation is divided into two blocks. The main and largest one serves to citrus fields primarily, and the other one to the block of vegetable fields. The citrus field block is divided into four sub-groups, alternating depending on the schedule. Hence, the system is configured in such a way that each field is irrigated 2 hours per day. On a regular day of watering, the pumping station is continuously working for 8 hours. The secondary block is supplied during 3-4 hours in the afternoon.

## **III. Energy demand**

The energy demand of the system responds to the irrigation schedule mentioned before. The frequency of these irrigations depends on the season of the year. During summer months it is usually to water six days a week; meanwhile, in winter the tendency is between 2-3 days a week. The electricity rate contracted with the marketer company is the 6.1A (high voltage, six periods).

## New profile consumption

The system was designed to cover afternoon consumption (Fig. 2). To take more profit of FV production, the irrigation schedule that was held during the afternoon will be switched earlier, during daily hours when irradiation is higher.

As it is shown in Figure 3, consumption is higher during summer months reaching on average 200 kW at dawn and early in the morning. Irradiance values are also higher in this season as show Figure 4, favouring the energy production in summer.

Figure 4: Monthly average solar irradiance.

Figure 3 shows the average daily consumption of the system distinguishing in winter and summer, with the afternoon consumption switched to earlier hours.

## **V. Devices**

## Floating system

The floating system chosen is composed of a floating structure with a fixed inclination angle of 5o. These floats are modular, and each one holds a panel. The maintenance platforms are strategically placed with corridors of maintenance.  Floats are made of HDPE ( _HighDensity Polyethylene)_ and can hold PV panels with the following range of dimensions: 16502120 mm length, 980-1060 mm width. [13]

Figure 3. Average daily consumption.

## PV panels

The chosen photovoltaic panel is the model AURORA SPLIT CELL – Monocrystalline PERC SR-M672400HL [14]. This type of panel uses the Half-Cut Cell technology, which consists of using photovoltaic cells shorter than conventional, connected internally in two series of strings. This allows to reduce the losses in the case of shadows, and the production of the panel is not cancelled. The technical characteristics of the panel are shown in Table III.

## Financial and viability results

The cost of the components is 72,757 € (Fig. 10), and the total cost of the system, including labour cost, contractual benefits, and VAT is 119,100 €.

Figure 10: Cost of the components.

The economic savings would be possible thanks to the reduction of energy consumption from the utility grid. But also due to the savings that would be generated thanks to the regulation established in the RD 244/2019. This regulation forces the marketer company to compensate economically the custom, due to the excess of energy injected to the utility grid.

In this project, the annual saving would be around 7,800 €. It is also considered a yearly saving of 353 € due to the savings by avoiding 80% of the evaporation of the water surface covered by the floating structure [3]. Additionally, according to the Valencian regulation (DOGV 25/5/2020), a bonus of 8,573 € will be obtained at year 10. The annual maintenance cost has been estimated in 1,200 €. The replacement of the inverter between the 1520 years is also considered.

The payback period is 15 years (Equation 12). The total profit at the end of the life of the installation would be 71,328 €.

## **IX. Conclusions**

According to the initial aim of the feasibility study of the photovoltaic installation with floating panels, it has been determined that it is technically viable to install a photovoltaic plant on the irrigation pool at the Cooperative under study. It is concluded that the final design of the photovoltaic system has 272 panels (108 kW), and one inverter of 100 kW.

Regarding the economic profitability, the payback period is 15 years, generating a profit of 71,327 € at year 25. This payback is not on the average for PV systems in Spain, as it is usually expected to obtain a return at 7-10 years. However, the extra cost due to the floating structure has increased the final budget.

Following the aim of energy saving, there is a reduction of the grid consumption of 55,707 kWh/year, equivalent to 13.55% of the total consumption. The saving could be improved if the demand were redistributed to the photovoltaic production times by increasing this energy-saving consumed from the utility grid.

The annual inflation is estimated at 1%. It is obtained an Internal Rate of Return of 4% annually for 25 years from equation (Equation 11), where NPC is the Net Present Cost and C0 is the initial cost of the FPV system.
